records.why: The worked example used the cosine rule, which is not taught in KICD Grade 10 (Sub-Strand 2.4 Trigonometry 1 covers only ratios of acute angles), and it used sines of obtuse angles. It now uses Pythagoras' theorem in the two right-angled triangles made by the common chord, then the cosine ratio of an acute angle, and the triangle area as chord half-length times distance (the same triangle as 1/2 r^2 sin 2 alpha). The old numbers were also slightly off (segments 485.8 and 662.3). Checked independently: x = (r1^2 - r2^2 + d^2)/(2d) = 2940/98 = 30; 42^2 - 30^2 = 864 = 35^2 - 19^2; angles 88.83 and 114.24 degrees (their halves sum with the angle at P, 78.46 degrees, to 180); segment A = 1367.44 - 881.82 = 485.62; segment B = 1221.28 - 558.48 = 662.79; total 1148.42 m2.
records.new: Step 2: Find where the common chord PQ crosses the line AB. PQ meets AB at right angles at a point M. Let AM = x, so MB = 49 − x, and let PM = h. Pythagoras in triangle APM: x² + h² = 42² = 1764. Pythagoras in triangle BPM: (49 − x)² + h² = 35² = 1225. Subtract: x² − (49 − x)² = 1764 − 1225 = 539, so 98x − 2401 = 539 and x = 2940/98 = 30 m. So AM = 30 m, MB = 19 m and h = √(1764 − 900) = √864 ≈ 29.39 m (check: √(1225 − 361) = √864). Step 3: Find the central angles with the cosine ratio of an acute angle (Sub-Strand 2.4): cos α = AM/AP = 30/42 ≈ 0.7143, so α ≈ 44.41° and angle PAQ = 2α ≈ 88.83°; cos β = MB/BP = 19/35 ≈ 0.5429, so β ≈ 57.12° and angle PBQ = 2β ≈ 114.24°. Step 4: Area of segment from Circle A = sector − triangle PAQ = (88.83/360) × π × 42² − PM × AM ≈ 0.24675 × 5541.77 − 29.39 × 30 ≈ 1367.4 − 881.8 ≈ 485.6 m² (the triangle area PM × AM is the same as ½r₁²sin 2α in the Lesson 5 formula). value.criterion: Selecting and stating the correct formula for each circle part

value.proficient: Meets Expectations: states the correct formula for most sub-regions, with only minor slips or limited explanation of why it fits.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: states few correct formulae or confuses them, for example omitting the triangle subtraction in the segment formula.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: all calculations are correct, with each radius squared before subtracting, angles used correctly, and answers given in the right units (m², cm², m).

value.developing: Approaches Expectations: several calculation errors, such as subtracting radii before squaring, or units missing or wrong.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: working is set out clearly step by step, and the steps for the lens (distance to the chord, central angles, two segments) are explained and linked to the segments.

value.developing: Approaches Expectations: working is hard to follow or answers are given without steps or reasons.

Audit item verified: the lessons use different pivot sizes for what is meant to be one farm. Lesson 1 outer/inner pipe 120 m / 80 m; Lesson 2 pipe 40 m; Lesson 3 pipe 21 m and garden 14 m; Lesson 4 rings 70 m / 40 m; Lesson 8 test 45 m / 30 m; Final Explanation 40 m / 25 m. The arithmetic in each lesson is correct, so I have not changed any numbers, only the running diagram (Lessons 2-3). A single dataset would mean recomputing about twenty answers; suggested option if you want it: use the Lesson 1 farm (outer 120 m, inner 80 m, sweep 120 degrees) everywhere, or tell learners in Lesson 1 that each lesson looks at a different pivot on the same farm. KICD suggests 12 lessons for Sub-Strand 2.6 (about 480 minutes at 40 minutes each); this sequence has 8 double lessons (640 minutes). Lesson 3 (arc length and sector perimeter) is not in the KICD content list for this sub-strand, so it is extra, and two KICD learning experiences are not taught except as the Lesson 7 extension I added: using a car wiper blade as the annular sector example, and the beaded necklace project. KICD says the number of lessons may vary, so I made no change. Teacher to decide whether to keep Lesson 3 and the 640 minutes. Sub-strand number and name match KICD (2.6 Area of a Part of a Circle).
